accident_report:
The crash occurred on a barrier divided east/west interstate in an interchange area.  Westbound where the crash took place there were three travel lanes with shoulders and barrier walls on the north and south sides.  Traffic counts indicate that the six total interstate lanes carry 75,954 vehicles per day at the crash site with a posted speed of 89kmph (55mph).  Conditions were daylight and dry on a weekday morning.

Vehicle #1 was a 2001 Ford Taurus traveling westbound in the far left lane.  Vehicle #2, a 2002 Chevrolet Cavalier, was westbound in the third lane ahead of Vehicle #1.  Apparently, the Taurus (V1) approached the Cavalier (V2) from behind at a high rate of speed and began following closely in an attempt to get the driver to move over and let him pass.  In an effort to get Vehicle #1 to increase its following distance the driver of Vehicle #2 tapped his brakes.  The Taurus (V1) changed lanes to the right and began to pass the Cavalier (V2).   Because there was a slower moving non-contact vehicle in the center lane ahead, Vehicle #1 then tried to return to the far left in front of Vehicle #2.  It appears that the Cavalier (V2) sped up as the Taurus (V1) was attempting change lanes to the left and the back left of Vehicle #1 contacted the right front of Vehicle #2.  The collision caused Vehicle #1 to rotate counterclockwise and it struck the left inside concrete retaining wall with its left side.  The Taurus (V1) came to rest on the north shoulder facing west.  After impact the Cavalier (V2) pulled over to the north shoulder.  Vehicle #1 was towed due to damage, and Vehicle #2 was driven away.

Vehicle #1 was driven by a 29-year-old male that was belted with no deployed airbags.  He was not injured in the crash.  In his statement he accused the other vehicle of aggressive driving.  Police charged him with failure to yield.

The Critical Precrash Event for Vehicle #1 was this vehicle over lane line on left side of travel lane.  The Critical Reason for the Critical Event was a decision error, misjudgment of gap or other's speed.  Some associated factors included misjudgment of other vehicles velocity.  Aggressive acts, speeding and tailgating, were coded and the driver was upset with other vehicle driver.  He had also taken some ibuprofen the day of the crash.

Vehicle #2 was operated by a 56-year-old male that was belted with no deployed airbags.  He was not injured in the crash.  In his statement he accused the other vehicle of aggressive driving.

The Critical Precrash Event for Vehicle #2 was other vehicle encroaching from adjacent lane over right lane line.  The Critical Reason for the Critical Event was not coded to this vehicle.  Some associated factors included aggressive acts, obstructing the path of other's and the driver was upset with the other vehicle driver.
